## Current Affiliation

Post-doctoral Reserarcher - Eurasia Institute of Earth Sciences, İstanbul Technical University, İstanbul, Turkey


## Research Profile

Hi, hi! This is Nurbahar Usta (you may also encounter Usta Baykal in publications or projects from 2019 - 2024; no worries, that's me too). My research, though somewhat delightfully scattered, gathers around forests: their ecology, conservation, management histories, and the many ways they are entangled with people. Much of my work has focused on the Kazdağları region and, in particular, Trojan fir forests. Over the years, this has involved systematic literature reviews, germination experiments, and recruitment dynamics modeling all of which, rather inconveniently and beautifully, produced more questions than answers. 

The more time I spent with forests, the more impossible it became to think of them as purely ecological systems. Forests are continuously shaped by governance, livelihoods, conflict, memory, policy, and politics just as much as by climate, soil, or species interactions. My current research therefore approaches the same landscapes through a socio-ecological lens, trying to understand forests not as isolated ecosystems, but as living assemblages of humans and more-than-humans.

Besides my current research projects, I am deeply interested in NGOs and their role in nature conservation in Turkey. I try to approach this field from both the outside and within: on one hand, by understanding the broader landscape of conservation efforts, environmental governance, and knowledge production; and on the other, by actively engaging through both volunteer and professional work.

And, like many millennials trying to remain emotionally functional under the age of multiple crisis, I also love running and joining book clubs.
